page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked up to 3.9 GHz, providing 48 burstable vCPUs across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The CPU subsystem features a 480 MB shared L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 384 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU memory-to-compute ratio.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for stateful persistence. Complementary public IPv4 addresses are not included, and baseline network throughput is rated at 11 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the high-speed memory interface demonstrates strong throughput, achieving 192.76 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block reads and 3,839.06 GB/sec in small cached reads. Cryptographic and vector extension workloads also exhibit solid performance, marked by 54,844.45 in PassMark encryption and strong multi-threaded compression metrics.

Compute-intensive execution tracks consistently in the upper quartile, showing strong multi-core Geekbench scores of 19,389 alongside strong software compilation and ray-tracing results. Due to hardware AMX instructions, small model language inference shows notable throughput, generating 343.17 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. The flex tier provides a cost-efficient resource profile by blending substantial memory density with burstable CPU limits, though workloads requiring steady non-throttled CPU saturation or bundled low-latency NVMe drives will encounter trade-offs.

This hardware footprint is suited for in-memory databases like Redis, which recorded 87.47 million set operations per second, as well as distributed caching layers, relational database hosting, large-scale static web serving, and memory-intensive ETL batch workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by a 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at up to 3.9 GHz with a 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 384 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an 11 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features burstable CPU allocation. Hardware-level support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 yields strong results across vector processing, encryption, and in-memory operations, including 87.47 million operations per second in Redis set benchmarks. Given its burstable execution tier and dense memory footprint, the instance offers a resource-efficient platform for Redis caches, relational database systems, memory-bound data transformations, and static web services that do not demand sustained continuous CPU ceiling capacity.
